title: Microwave-assisted synthesis of thioether-linked sulfonamides as dual DHPS/DHFR inhibitors: biological evaluation and molecular dynamics studies
content: The increasing burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) highlights the need for structurally diverse antibacterial agents targeting established bacterial pathways. Sulfonamides and diaminopyrimidines inhibit successive enzymes in bacterial folate biosynthesis, dihydropteroate synthase (DHPS) and dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), respectively. The emergence of resistant bacterial strains motivates the development of molecular frameworks capable of inhibiting both enzymes. This study investigated the molecular hybridisation of sulfonamide and thiol-containing heterocyclic pharmacophores to develop antibacterial candidates with potential dual DHPS/DHFR inhibitory activity. Eight thioether-linked sulfonamide derivatives (4a–d and 6a–d) were synthesised using microwave-assisted heating, achieving 92–95% yields within 7–10 min. Antibacterial evaluation against Gram-positive and Gram-negative strains, including clinical methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), identified compound 4a as the most active derivative against MRSA (MIC = 2 µg mL−1). Enzyme inhibition assays confirmed inhibitory activity against both DHPS and DHFR for compounds 4a and 6a. Compound 4a exhibited IC50 values of 0.6464 and 0.4196 µg mL−1 against DHPS and DHFR, respectively, compared with 1.4815 and 0.8415 µg mL−1 for compound 6a. Molecular docking, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM-GBSA, and conformational analyses provided insights into the interactions and dynamics of the 4a-DHPS and 4a-DHFR complexes. Compound 4a additionally demonstrated DPPH radical-scavenging activity comparable to ascorbic acid, limited cytotoxicity under tested conditions, and DNA association without pronounced cleavage. ADMET predictions provided preliminary pharmacokinetic and toxicity insights. Taken together, these results identify compound 4a as a promising antibacterial lead with inhibitory activity against both DHPS and DHFR, supporting its further investigation.
